edges.description: Loss of lysosomal alpha-NAGA exoglycosidase activity prevents cleavage of terminal alpha-GalNAc residues from O-linked glycopeptides.
Lysosomal glycopeptide accumulation leads to cellular vacuolization and upper-dermal vascular ectasia underlying cutaneous angiokeratomas.
edges.target: Superficial Dermal Vascular Ectasia and Vacuolization

edges.description: Systemic alpha-NAGA deficiency and glycopeptide accumulation lead through uncharacterized peripheral nerve intermediates to axonal and demyelinating polyneuropathy.
Systemic glycopeptide accumulation leads through uncharacterized auditory-pathway intermediates to sensorineural hearing impairment.
Systemic glycopeptide accumulation leads through uncharacterized vestibular intermediates to recurrent vertigo attacks.
Systemic glycopeptide storage contributes through uncharacterized intermediates to chronic progressive lymphedema.
Systemic glycopeptide storage contributes through uncharacterized intermediates to coarse facial features.
Alpha-NAGA deficiency and glycopeptide accumulation are associated through uncharacterized intermediates with mild cognitive impairment in the adult-onset form.
Systemic glycopeptide accumulation can lead through uncharacterized myocardial intermediates to moderate cardiomegaly.
Systemic glycopeptide accumulation can lead through uncharacterized myocardial intermediates to hypertrophy of the interventricular septum.
Ectatic upper-dermal vessels with overlying epidermal acanthosis and hyperkeratosis manifest clinically as diffuse cutaneous angiokeratomas.
edges.source: Superficial Dermal Vascular Ectasia and Vacuolization

nodes.description: Biallelic NAGA loss-of-function variants (such as p.Arg329Trp, p.Arg329Gln, or p.Glu193*) destabilize the homodimeric lysosomal exoglycosidase or truncate the polypeptide, abolishing removal of terminal alpha-N-acetylgalactosamine residues from O-linked glycopeptides and glycolipids.
